question: What is the primary clinical goal of Post-Abortion Care in healthcare facilities?

options.A: Providing routine antenatal screening for pregnant women
options.B: Reducing maternal morbidity and mortality from abortion complications

explanation: Post-Abortion Care is specifically structured to treat emergency complications arising from incomplete or unsafe pregnancy terminations, thereby lowering maternal death rates. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h1)

question: Why does Post-Abortion Care include services for spontaneous miscarriages alongside induced abortions?

options.A: Spontaneous miscarriages never require medical or surgical intervention
options.B: Hospitals lack the capacity to differentiate between the two causes of bleeding
options.C: Both conditions present with identical clinical management needs for incomplete tissue expulsion
options.D: Health policies mandate separate wards for miscarriage and abortion patients

explanation: Whether a pregnancy loss is spontaneous or induced, the physiological presentation of incomplete tissue and bleeding requires the same emergency stabilization and evacuation protocols. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five core elements of Post-Abortion Care?
explanation: Routine childhood immunizations are part of child health services, not the five designated core elements of Post-Abortion Care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h2)

question: At what point in the care timeline should contraceptive services be introduced to a PAC client?

options.A: Exclusively when requested during a routine annual physical
options.B: During the child welfare clinic visit a year later
options.C: Before discharge while still receiving care at the facility
options.D: Only after six months of complete sexual abstinence

explanation: Fertility returns very rapidly after a pregnancy loss, making immediate in-facility family planning provision essential before discharge. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h2)

question: What are the two primary methods used for uterine evacuation in first-trimester incomplete abortions?

options.A: External cephalic version and continuous electronic monitoring
options.B: Total abdominal hysterectomy and diagnostic laparoscopy
options.C: Manual Vacuum Aspiration and medical management with misoprostol
options.D: Radiation therapy and radical pelvic lymph node dissection

explanation: Manual Vacuum Aspiration and misoprostol are the standard, evidence-based interventions for clearing retained products of conception safely in the first trimester. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h3)

question: A PAC client presents with lower abdominal tenderness, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and a temperature of 38.5°C. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Schedule an elective follow-up appointment for two months later
options.B: Commence broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics and notify the clinician
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately with oral pain relievers
options.D: Advise the client to perform daily sitz baths at home

explanation: Fever, foul discharge, and tenderness indicate pelvic infection, requiring prompt antibiotic therapy and medical review to prevent sepsis. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h3)

question: Which quality is most essential for a nurse providing post-abortion counseling?

options.A: Rushing the patient through the discharge process
options.C: Minimizing the emotional impact of the loss

explanation: Establishing trust through confidentiality and a non-judgmental demeanor encourages patients to share concerns and accept necessary follow-up care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h4)

question: Why is it important to discuss expected physical symptoms like mild cramping during counseling before discharge?

options.A: It guarantees the client will never experience any pain whatsoever
options.B: It prevents unnecessary panic over normal post-procedure recovery signs
options.C: It replaces the need for prescribing any analgesic medications
options.D: It ensures the patient remains admitted in the hospital ward longer

explanation: Educating clients on normal bodily responses helps them differentiate between expected healing processes and dangerous complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h4)

question: How soon can ovulation return following an abortion procedure?

options.D: Only after a normal menstrual cycle occurs

explanation: Because follicular development resumes quickly, a woman can become pregnant again very soon after an abortion if contraception is not adopted immediately. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h5)

question: What does providing a comprehensive method mix during PAC entail?

options.A: Mandating that every patient receive a specific hormonal injection
options.B: Restricting choices exclusively to barrier methods like male condoms
options.C: Requiring spousal consent before dispensing any birth control
options.D: Offering a variety of short and long-acting contraceptive choices for voluntary selection

explanation: A comprehensive method mix provides diverse options so patients can choose the method that best fits their personal health profile and future plans. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of reproductive health linkages in PAC?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any follow-up clinical appointments
options.B: Replacing emergency medical wards with rural community centers
options.C: Connecting clients to broader services like STI screening and cancer checks
options.D: Mandating compulsory surgical interventions for all discharged patients

explanation: Linkages ensure that clients receive holistic care that extends beyond the immediate abortion complication to address wider health needs. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h6)

question: How do community outreach programs assist in improving post-abortion health outcomes?

options.A: By educating the public on danger signs and reducing barriers to safe care
options.B: By penalizing individuals who experience spontaneous miscarriages
options.C: By replacing hospital-based doctors with traditional birth attendants
options.D: By performing surgical uterine evacuations inside local village squares

explanation: Community education empowers people to recognize complications early and seek professional help promptly, reducing severe morbidity. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h6)

question: What is a core ethical duty of nurses when providing Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality and non-discriminatory care
options.B: Reporting all PAC clients to law enforcement agencies
options.C: Publicly disclosing patient diagnoses to the community
options.D: Refusing treatment based on personal religious beliefs

explanation: Nurses are ethically bound to treat all patients with dignity, ensuring privacy and equal standards of care free from personal bias. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h7)

question: How does healthcare stigma negatively impact patients requiring post-abortion care?

options.A: It improves the overall speed of physical recovery and wound healing
options.B: It encourages patients to attend hospital follow-up visits more frequently
options.C: It deters individuals from seeking timely treatment, leading to severe complications
options.D: It eliminates the need for any form of psychological counseling

explanation: Fear of judgment and hostility causes many women to delay seeking care until their conditions become life-threatening. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h7)
